hypotheses.reasoning: A routine rolling deploy of auth-svc v5.17.0 (#152) drained auth-svc-2 at 22:24:39 and dropped capacity to 3/4 (#154). On its own that should have been survivable. Logins were succeeding right up to it (#150, #156). Within seconds, account-svc's AuthClient started retrying 503s straight away, up to 4 attempts, with backoff turned off (#159, #167, #178, #187). Inbound load on auth-svc then climbed to 3.2x, 4.1x and 5.0x baseline (#175, #186, #198). auth-svc shed that load with 503s because its queue was full (#174, #191), and the shed requests triggered more retries. The loop keeps itself going, which is why the 503 rate is not recovering even though the trigger was small. Edge-proxy 503s (#162 onward) are downstream symptoms. Unrelated noise: edge-proxy disk at 81% (#68), the slow audit_log query (#148), audit-consumer GC pauses (#144) and the accounts vacuum (#158).

The onset lines up with the auth-svc v5.17.0 rollout. But the only auth-svc errors are load-shed 503s that rise with request rate, and there is no sign of bugs in the new version, so the release looks like the trigger rather than the fault.

verdict.recommendedAction: Turn exponential backoff with jitter back on in account-svc's AuthClient, or drop the retry count to 1, and add a retry budget or circuit breaker. To break the loop now, rate-limit /login at edge-proxy or add auth-svc capacity until the extra load drains. Pause the auth-svc rollout until retries are fixed, and size rollouts so that losing one instance leaves enough headroom.
